title: Flashback Friday: Is Organic Meat Less Carcinogenic?
summary: Reviews a study finding organic and conventional meat carry similar levels of carcinogenic persistent pollutants.

assertions.quote: the consumption of organic meat does not diminish the carcinogenic potential associated with the intake of these pollutants

verdicts.note: A Spanish study found minimal differences in persistent pollutants between organic and conventional meat, but the evidence comes from very few studies.
Too few data sets existed for toxic metals (As, Pb, Cd) and pesticides in meat to draw conclusions, so the review cannot compare contaminant loads.

assertions.quote: meat, fish, and dairy believed to contribute almost all of the dioxin body exposure
Certified organic meat comes from livestock that are fed with organically produced feed that is free of pesticides and animal by-products, by law.

verdicts.note: 7 CFR 205.237 requires 100 percent organic feed and bans mammalian and poultry by-products.

7 CFR 205.237(a) requires a total feed ration of certified organic agricultural products, pasture and forage included, with allowed synthetic additives and supplements and narrow exceptions for transitioning dairy and breeder stock.
ERS notes organic livestock farmers must provide organic feed and pasture land, which it cites as a driver of high dairy and egg premiums.
